newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: BCP, J.Martins higher on bank news.
newsitem.headline: BCP, J.Martins higher on bank news.

text.p: Shares in Portugal's biggest private bank, Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), and second largest retailer Jeronimo Martins opened higher after the groups said they had signed an agreement to launch a new bank.
BCP traded at 1,860 escudos, up 30, and JM stood at 14,600 escudos, up 400, at 0911 GMT.
"There is little liquidity in BCP, but its first reaction was to jump to 1,869 escudos on the news of the agreement with JM," said one operator.
Another said: "The market is still digesting the agreement, but BCP shares could rise to 1,900 escudos because there is a favourable view towards JM buying BCP shares."

JM and BCP said on Wednesday that they had signed an agreement to launch a private bank owned equally by both groups that would offer in-store financial services to customers in JM hypermarkets and supermarkets.
JM would like to buy gradually up to 1.5 percent of BCP, JM Finance Director Jorge Ponce de Leao told Reuters.
